title: Ethiopian Ye-Abesha Gomen Sauce
community: All of Ethiopia — collard green purée as sauce
author: Mama Tigist
desc: Ethiopian Collard Green Sauce — blanched collard greens sautéed with garlic and onion, then roughly puréed into a thick, deeply green sauce used as a condiment alongside kitfo, tibs, and the celebration platter. The green element in liquid form.
longDesc: Collard green sauce is Gomen (ETH106) taken one step further — after sautéing, the greens are roughly puréed into a thick sauce that can be used as a condiment, spooned over injera, or used as the green base for a celebratory platter.
steps: Blanch collard greens 3 minutes. Drain and squeeze dry.
Heat oil. Cook onion and garlic until golden.
Cool slightly. Blend roughly — leave some texture.
chefTips: Squeeze excess water from greens before blending.
commonMistakes: Too smooth — loses the identity of collard greens.
Not squeezing out water — watery sauce.
cookingScience: See ETH106 for collard green science.
healthBenefits: Concentrated vitamins K, A, and C from greens.
culturalNote: Gomen sauce is Gomen elevated to a condiment — the same greens, the same garlic, but transformed into a format that accompanies kitfo at the most sophisticated Ethiopian tables.
